numerical_failure.observed_behavior: The UTC offset is applied with a bare int64 add, so a UTC instant whose local wall time leaves the representable range wraps silently by about 585 years. For pd.DatetimeIndex([pd.Timestamp.min], tz='UTC').tz_convert('US/Pacific').tz_localize(None) the result is '2262-04-11 15:54:18.854775809'. tz_localize(None), floor/ceil/round, .year and strftime all report the wrapped value. A local value equal to the NaT sentinel

numerical_characteristics.precision: nanosecond (int64 i8 storage; local value equal to iNaT sentinel at ns freq)
numerical_characteristics.magnitude: Timestamp.max / Timestamp.min scale; wrap of roughly 585 years; sentinel value iNaT (int64 min)
category_specific_evidence: Localizer.utc_val_to_local_val used a bare add, so a UTC instant whose local wall time leaves the representable int64 range wrapped by about 585 years instead of raising OutOfBoundsDatetime

Reproducer: pd.DatetimeIndex([pd.Timestamp.min], tz='UTC').tz_convert('US/Pacific').tz_localize(None) gives '2262-04-11 15:54:18.854775809' (585 years off), while pd.Timestamp(pd.Timestamp.min._value, tz='UTC').tz_convert('US/Pacific') raises OutOfBoundsDatetime 'overflows past'
Local value exactly equal to the NaT sentinel (iNaT) is stored back as NaT; at nanosecond freq the period ordinal equals the local i8 value so a local time on the sentinel becomes NaT
Issue reproducer: DatetimeIndex from Timestamp(iNaT + 3600*10**9, tz='UTC') converted to fixed offset timezone(timedelta(hours=-1)) yields local value equal to iNaT

Out-of-bounds read of info.deltas[ntrans] in the nonexistent='shift' path when bisect_right_i8 returns ntrans; clamping to ntrans-1 is stated to be incorrect; example Asia/Anadyr 2011-03-27 02:30 with nonexistent='shift_backward' is an hour out

Fix adds raise_out_of_bounds(local_val, BS_UNDERFLOW, reso) when stored value equals NPY_NAT in tz_convert_from_utc and dt64arr_to_periodarr; sentinel left alone in the shift itself to avoid regressing to_pydatetime, astype(object), and coarser-freq to_period
Regression test test_dti_utc_to_local_overflow parametrized over Europe/Berlin (zoneinfo), dateutil gettz Europe/Berlin, and Etc/GMT-9 expects OutOfBoundsDatetime match 'overflows past'
reproduction_risks: Result depends on memory contents when deltas[ntrans] is read out of bounds, so results can differ between calls in the same process
Eager scalar constructor refuses the conversion, so the reproducer must build the UTC index without the scalar path (e.g., via i8 view and tz_localize)
Clamping the bisect index to ntrans-1 gives wrong results for zones east of UTC because the bisect compares wall time to UTC instants
Coarser-frequency to_period, to_pydatetime and astype(object) rely on sentinel-valued local times rendering correctly, so rejecting at the shift level would regress them
